tasks.title: Discover Recurring Code Abstractions and Patterns
tasks.description: Automatically surface useful abstractions, naming patterns, and architectural idioms from the codebase and recent changes.
tasks.details:
Lightweight concept mining for code.
- Scan recent patches, files, and task outcomes for repeated structures.
- Propose named abstractions or conventions when they appear multiple times.
- Store them in a simple, queryable form (OKF or local index).
- Use discovered patterns to improve future code generation suggestions.
- Keep scope to this project — no wild cross-domain claims.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. The system identifies at least 2-3 meaningful recurring patterns per significant batch of changes.
2. Discovered abstractions are human-readable and actionable.
3. Using the discovered patterns measurably improves suggestion quality in later tasks.

tasks.title: Mine Common Improvement Patterns from Task History
tasks.description: Extract recurring successful (and unsuccessful) approaches from past tasks, patches, and reviews.
tasks.details:
Practical pattern mining for a coding agent.
- Focus on code changes, debugging steps, refactor types, and testing approaches.
- Cluster similar successful tactics.
- Represent patterns simply (e.g. 'when you see X, try Y').
- Make patterns available during planning and code generation.
- Track which patterns correlate with better outcomes.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. System can surface 5-10 high-frequency patterns from history.
2. Patterns are specific enough to be applied by the agent.
3. Using mined patterns improves task success rate or reduces iterations in experiments.

tasks.title: Apply Mined Patterns During Code Changes
tasks.description: Use discovered patterns to guide or validate code generation and refactoring.
tasks.details:
Pattern application layer.
- Before making changes, check against known good patterns.
- Suggest applying relevant patterns when appropriate.
- After changes, check whether known patterns were followed or violated.
- Allow easy override and learning from exceptions.
- Start with read-only suggestions before any automatic application.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Relevant patterns are surfaced during realistic coding tasks.
2. Pattern suggestions are accepted at a reasonable rate.
3. Following patterns correlates with fewer review comments or faster task completion.

tasks.title: Analyze Tool Usage and Suggest Improvements
tasks.description: Review how tools are actually used and propose practical improvements to tool design or prompts.
tasks.details:
Grounded tool evolution.
- Collect telemetry on tool calls, success/failure rates, and common errors.
- Identify frequently misused, underused, or painful tools.
- Generate concrete suggestions (better descriptions, parameter changes, new helper tools, prompt adjustments).
- Keep all suggestions human-reviewable.
- Do not allow fully autonomous tool creation or deletion yet.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Usage data is collected automatically.
2. The system produces at least a few actionable tool improvement proposals from real usage.
3. Implemented suggestions reduce tool-related failures or friction.

tasks.title: Implement Task 411: Evaluation-Driven Self-Improvement Loop
tasks.description: Grounded self-improvement: Turn evaluation results, improvement_suggestions, and task outcomes into concrete, reviewable proposals for prompts, heuristics, and agent behavior. Start simple and human-review gated.
tasks.details: Completed: Added SelfImprovementProposal type, generate_self_improvement_proposals() in new self_improvement.rs module. Wired generation into outer_loop after evaluation. Proposals are logged, stored in HOHPlan, and are concrete/reviewable (prompt tweaks, heuristic changes, test_strategy enforcement, patch quality). All changes human-gated. Updated state + planner fallbacks.
tasks.testStrategy: After running a HOH iteration, the system should surface at least 2-3 concrete self-improvement proposals in logs or state. Proposals should be specific and actionable.

tasks.title: Design multi-slot /replace memory specification
tasks.description: Define the structure, naming rules, and indexing format for multi-slot /replace memory blocks.
tasks.details: Core structures fully implemented and tested (451-453). Design embodied in MemorySlot, SlotType, MemoryManager, and compaction. All relevant tests pass.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify the spec is complete, unambiguous, and covers naming, indexing, limits, and promotion rules. Validate with example memory blocks.

tasks.title: Implement Rust MemorySlot struct
tasks.description: Create the Rust struct representing a single /replace memory slot.
tasks.details: Fully implemented in src/memory/replace_slot.rs with MemorySlot + SlotType, update/append, token_count, compact, summarize, promote_to_okf, and tests.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test struct creation, updating, token counting, and summarization. Ensure max_tokens enforcement works.

tasks.title: Implement MemoryManager for multi-slot system
tasks.description: Create a manager that handles multiple named and indexed /replace memory slots.
tasks.details: Fully implemented in src/memory/memory_manager.rs: named slots (plan/working/context/errors), indexed mem.N slots, update_slot, get_slot, compact_all (priority order), evict_oldest, serialize_for_prompt, promote_all stub, auto-compaction, and unit tests.
tasks.testStrategy: Test adding, updating, compacting, and promoting slots. Validate serialization output matches prompt builder requirements.

tasks.title: Implement context compaction algorithm
tasks.description: Create the algorithm that summarizes older memory blocks and reduces token usage.
tasks.details: Full deterministic compaction implemented in src/memory/compaction.rs with 8-step pipeline, slot-specific rules, integrated into MemorySlot and MemoryManager. All tests pass.
tasks.testStrategy: Feed large memory sets and verify compaction reduces tokens by 50–80% while preserving meaning. Validate deterministic output.

tasks.title: Integrate MemoryManager into agent loop
tasks.description: Modify the Rust agent loop to use multi-slot /replace memory.
tasks.details: MemoryManager and slots exist but not yet integrated into the main agent loop, prompt builder, or recursive invoke paths.
tasks.testStrategy: Run simulated agent loops and verify memory updates, compaction, and prompt injection work correctly. Validate no runaway context growth.

tasks.title: Update prompt builder to include named memory slots
tasks.description: Modify prompt builder to inject multi-slot /replace blocks into the LLM prompt.
tasks.details:
Update prompt builder:
- Add sections for each slot: plan, working, context, errors
- Add indexed blocks: mem.0, mem.1, mem.2
- Ensure consistent formatting
- Ensure LLM instructions explain how to use slots
- Add token budgeting logic
tasks.testStrategy: Verify prompt output includes all slots in correct order. Validate formatting and token budgeting.

tasks.title: Implement OKF promotion pipeline
tasks.description: Add logic to promote important memory facts into OKF bundles.
tasks.details:
Implement promotion rules:
- Detect stable facts
- Detect repeated patterns
- Detect long-term relevance
- Write promoted facts into OKF bundles via Helix
- Remove promoted content from short-term memory
tasks.testStrategy: Test promotion with simulated memory. Verify OKF bundles update correctly and memory shrinks.

tasks.title: Add LLM instructions for multi-slot memory
tasks.description: Update system prompt to teach the LLM how to use named and indexed memory slots.
tasks.details:
Add instructions:
- Explain each slot: plan, working, context, errors
- Explain indexed slots: mem.0, mem.1, mem.2
- Explain update rules
- Explain compaction behavior
- Explain OKF promotion
- Provide usage examples
tasks.testStrategy: Run LLM tests verifying correct usage of memory slots. Validate no hallucinated slot names.

tasks.title: End-to-end integration test
tasks.description: Test the full multi-slot memory system inside the coding agent.
tasks.details:
Perform full integration test:

- Verify memory updates
- Verify compaction
- Verify OKF promotion
- Verify prompt injection
- Verify cost reduction
- Verify stability across recursive invoke() calls
tasks.testStrategy: Run long-horizon coding tasks and confirm stable behavior, reduced context size, and correct memory usage.

tasks.title: Document multi-slot memory system

tasks.details:
Document:

tasks.testStrategy: Verify documentation is complete, accurate, and matches implementation.

tasks.title: Complete /handoffs Slash Command Wiring and Handoff Logging Integration (Code Review Follow-up)
tasks.description: Finish the integration of the /handoffs feature (Tasks 418/419) so the command is advertised, dispatched, auto-logs on every planner step, appears in status bar, and exposes analysis programmatically for HOH.
tasks.details:
Code review (post-418/419) identified critical gaps:
- /handoffs not present in get_available_commands() (invisible in Zed picker)
- BuiltinResult::ShowHandoffs never handled in handle_builtin_result (acp.rs + chat.rs)
- Exhaustiveness test in slash_commands.rs is missing the variant (repeat of ReplaceMemory bug)
- log_role_handoff() and log_handoff() have almost zero callers
- No status bar integration

Confirmed decisions from review:
- Command variant: BuiltinResult::ShowHandoffs
- Persistence: session snapshot only (no extra OKF/persistence for now)
- Auto-log aggressiveness: log a handoff on every planner step + role switches + agent spawns/delegates
- Programmatic access: expose structured analysis (not just string) for HOH consumption
- UI: show a short handoff summary in the status bar when events exist

Scope of work:
1. Add "handoffs" entry to get_available_commands() (with good description).
2. Implement handling for BuiltinResult::ShowHandoffs in acp.rs handle_builtin_result (call get_handoff_log).
3. Wire the same in CLI interactive chat slash handler.
4. Fix the builtin_result_is_exhaustive test (and any other match sites).
5. Call log_role_handoff from actual role switch paths.
6. Add auto-log calls on planner steps (and key spawn/delegate points).
7. Add programmatic API (e.g. get_handoff_analysis or expose HandoffAnalysis) for HOH.
8. Surface short summary in status bar (emit_context_and_status / status_bar paths).
9. Add/update tests (unit for analysis, integration for full command flow).
10. Update task 418/419 descriptions to note wiring completed in 462.

Keep the design lightweight and session-scoped as originally implemented in handoff.rs.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. /handoffs appears in ACP available commands, /help, and Zed slash picker.
2. /handoffs in both ACP and CLI returns useful markdown including total, empty-context warnings, role switches, and most-common pair.
3. Role switches automatically produce HandoffEvent entries.
4. Planner steps (and at least one spawn/delegate) automatically log handoffs.
5. Exhaustiveness test compiles cleanly and covers ShowHandoffs.
6. HOH code can call a new get_handoff_analysis() (or equivalent) and receive structured data (not just string).
7. Status bar shows a short handoff indicator/summary when events exist.
8. Session save/load round-trips the handoffs vec correctly.
9. No regression in other slash commands (full test suite for slash_commands + handle_builtin_result).
10. cargo test + cargo check clean.
